A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: GP direct access to low-dose CT. Health-centre doctors can order chest CT directly for patients whose symptoms raise suspicion but do not meet urgent referral criteria, without first referring to specialist care.
effect_summary_en: The Danish trial found a non-significant 8-day shorter median diagnostic interval (36 vs 44 days, p=0.299).
supported_en: BMC Cancer 2015 (Aarhus trial): direct GP access to low-dose CT came with an 8-day shorter median diagnostic interval (36 vs 44 days), not statistically significant.
not_supported_en: The trial does not show a reliable 8-day gain or any effect on time to treatment start, and no Satakunta results are published yet.

in_use_summary_en: Satakunnan Kansa reports that since 2024 Satakunta's primary care has routinely referred patients with suspected lung cancer (at least 20 pack-years plus symptoms) directly to chest CT, after a pilot that began in 2022; about 170 patients have been scanned.
summary_en: Satakunnan Kansa (11 Nov 2026) reports that Satakunta wellbeing services county lets primary-care doctors send patients with suspected lung cancer straight to chest CT. Patients qualify if they have at least 20 pack-years of smoking and symptoms. The service began as a pilot in 2022, became routine in 2024, and about 170 patients have been scanned so far. The Danish cluster-randomised trial (BMC Cancer 2015) found a median diagnostic interval of 36 days with direct CT access against 44 days without (p=0.299), so the 8-day difference is not statistically significant.
unanswered_en: I found no page from the county itself confirming the pathway, only the newspaper report, and the county's own study of how well it works has not been published.
